Explain the biochemical interaction and molecular mechanism between the drug 'Imatinib', the biological target 'ABL1', and the pathological condition 'Chronic Myeloid Leukemia'.
Detail the specific binding mechanism, affinity, and clinical therapeutic rationale.
Be specific and concise (3-5 sentences).
text: In Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML), the pathognomonic $t(9;22)$ translocation creates the constitutively active BCR-ABL1 chimeric tyrosine kinase, which drives aberrant granulocyte proliferation via continuous autophosphorylation and downstream signaling. Imatinib functions as a highly selective, competitive antagonist that binds to the ATP-binding pocket of the ABL1 kinase domain specifically when the protein is in its inactive, "DFG-out" conformation. This binding is stabilized by critical hydrogen bonds with residues Glu286 and Asp381, as well as hydrophobic interactions with the gatekeeper residue Thr315, exhibiting a high binding affinity ($K_i \approx 10\text{ nM}$). By blocking ATP binding, Imatinib prevents the phosphorylation of substrate proteins, effectively arresting oncogenic signaling cascades (such as JAK/STAT, PI3K/AKT, and MAPK/ERK) to induce apoptosis in leukemic clones and achieve deep molecular remission in CML patients.
